notes: WHEN A RECORDING IS INTERRUPTED, THE LEDGER NOW TELLS YOU — AND FINISHES THE JOB. This update carries two releases; coming from 0.8.77 you get both. Recording money is a short chain: the ledger entry posts, then the cheque, lodgement, invoice, bill or register entry that goes with it is written. If the machine sleeps or something fails between the two, the books have moved and the paperwork has not — and the screen used to look as though nothing had happened, so recording it again was the obvious thing to do, and that is what pays a supplier twice. Receipts, Payments, Bank Transfers, Petty Cash and Payroll now name the half-finished job wherever the money has already moved, and offer to complete the ORIGINAL entry rather than repeat it. Invoices and Vendor Bills refuse a second receipt or payment over a stranded one and send you to Undo receipts / Undo payments, which reverses it cleanly so it can be recorded once, properly. WHAT YOU ARE OWED AND WHAT YOU OWE ARE NOW CHECKED AS A WHOLE. The checks banner adds up every outstanding invoice and every outstanding bill and compares each against its control account, so any difference is named as soon as it appears — not just the obvious case where a document had counted nothing at all. That gap mattered: a bill settled twice with only one settlement recorded still read as partly settled, and your payables quietly sat below what your bills actually said. Invoices and bills in foreign currency are compared exactly, using the figures your ledger posted rather than a rate worked out again afterwards, and month-end revaluations and opening balances are set aside instead of being reported as errors. THREE THINGS THAT HAD NO WAY BACK NOW HAVE ONE. A credit or debit note that posted without its record being written is named on the screen with a Record it button, rebuilt from the ledger entry; until now it was only found if you happened to open the note dialog on that same document, and the invoice meanwhile overstated what was owed to you. Petty-cash vouchers stuck on a reimbursement that never went through can be handed back to pending — they had been disappearing from the reimbursable list, leaving the float impossible to close. And a commitment a posted payment never drew down can be drawn from the payment itself, so your budget stops holding money you have already spent. NO DATABASE CHANGE in either release: your data and settings are untouched, and you install straight over the old version. Please still take a backup first — Backup & Export, Back up now.
